title: Source Documents
summary: Why source documents are needed, the main source documents for cash transactions (receipts, cash register rolls, deposit slips, cheque counterfoils, EFT notices) and the information they contain.

notes.text: The original written or electronic proof that a transaction has taken place. It provides the information that is recorded in the journals.

items: It is **proof** of the transaction for the owner, auditors and SARS.
It gives the details needed for recording: date, amount, names and what was paid or received.
Businesses must keep source documents for at least **five years**.

rows: When the business receives money (cash or EFT) from someone, e.g. a client paying for services or the owner contributing capital
The original goes to the payer; the business keeps the **duplicate** as its source document
Records all cash sales or services for the day in a shop
The business keeps the till roll
When cash received is deposited into the business's bank account
The bank stamps the copy for the business
When the business pays by cheque; the counterfoil stays in the cheque book as a record. (Cheques are no longer used by most South African banks, but you may still see them in exercises.)
EFT payment notice / proof of payment
When the business pays electronically by **Electronic Funds Transfer**
Shows debit orders, bank charges and interest deducted by the bank
Received when the business buys something with cash

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Each document is numbered. When a source document is entered in a journal, its **number** is written in the 'Doc' column, so that the entry can always be traced back.

notes.title: Example: Receipt no. 014
notes.text:
THANDI'S HAIR SALON
12 Long Street, Mthatha
Receipt no. 014                Date: 5 March 2025
Received from: N. Dlamini
The sum of: Four hundred and fifty rand only
For: Hair treatment
Amount: R450,00
Signed: T. Mbeki (owner)

items: The name and address of the business
The amount in words and in figures
Signature of the person receiving the money

notes.title: Choosing the correct source document
notes.problem: Which source document is used for each transaction? (a) The owner contributes R20 000 cash as capital. (b) The business pays the telephone account by EFT. (c) Cash for services rendered in a day is rung up on the till.
steps: (b) EFT payment notice / proof of payment.

questions.prompt: Give THREE reasons why source documents are important.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): proof of transactions; provide details for recording; prevent fraud/theft; needed by auditors and SARS; allow entries to be traced

questions.prompt: Name THREE details that must appear on a receipt.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): business name/address; receipt number; date; received from; amount in words and figures; reason for payment; signature
